short: ASR transcripts as training labels (M02) are standard: Afouras 2020 and the group's 2022 paper did it; scale lowers LRS3 VSR WER to 19.1%, but single runs and USR 2.0 (17.6%) weaken the claim.
position: Auto-AVSR [@ma2023autoavsr] changes one component, the training labels (M02), adding 2,630 h of AVSpeech and VoxCeleb2 transcribed by a public ASR model. The design is standard: Afouras et al. trained lip readers with CTC on ASR-generated transcripts of unlabelled video [@afouras2020asr], and the same group had already added AVSpeech with automatically generated transcriptions [@ma2022multilingual]; what the paper adds is scale (641 h to 2,630 h) and a comparison of four labellers. The scale result holds: LRS3 visual-only WER falls from 33.0% to 19.1% as automatic-label hours grow (Table 2), though the [later] USR 2.0 reaches 17.6% on the same two corpora with self-generated labels [@haliassos2026usr2]. Evaluation (M12) drops the ten-run means of the group's prior work [@ma2022multilingual], so the labeller ranking (Table 1) and the unanchored 30% headline carry less weight than claimed.
